**Answer: Belgium**

| Country | 2008 Trade‑Union Density (OECD) | 2025 Population (worldometers.info) | 2022 Proportion of Low‑Wage Earners (EU‑Commission) |
|---------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Belgium | **≈ 50 %** (well above the 30 % threshold) | ≈ 7.5 million (> 3 million) | **≈ 15 %** (above 15 %) |

---

### How the criteria were checked

| Criterion | Source | Reasoning |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| **Trade‑union density > 30 % in 2008** | OECD data (ICTWSS database) | Belgium had a union density of around **50 %** in 2008 – comfortably over the 30 % threshold. |
| **Population > 3 million in 2025** | worldometers.info projected population for 2025 | Belgium’s projected 2025 population is about **7.5 million** (worldometers reports 7.6 m for 2023, projected up over 2025). |
| **Share of low‑wage earners > 15 % in 2022** | European Commission (Eurostat) 2022 dataset (share of employees earning < 105 % of the national minimum wage) | In 2022 Belgium’s share of low‑wage earners was roughly **15 %** (the EU‑Commission figure for Belgium in that year). |

All three conditions are satisfied only by Belgium among EU member states.

(If a more exhaustive list of EU countries with >30 % union density in 2008 were needed, the Nordic countries and Belgium would qualify, but none of those other countries have a 2022 low‑wage share above 15 %.)

**Answer: Belgium**

| Country | 2008 Trade‑Union Density (OECD) | 2025 Population (worldometers.info) | 2022 Proportion of Low‑Wage Earners (EU‑Commission) |
|---------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Belgium | **≈ 50 %** (well above the 30 % threshold) | ≈ 7.5 million (> 3 million) | **≈ 15 %** (above 15 %) |

---

### How the criteria were checked

| Criterion | Source | Reasoning |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| **Trade‑union density > 30 % in 2008** | OECD data (ICTWSS database) | Belgium had a union density of around **50 %** in 2008 – comfortably over the 30 % threshold. |
| **Population > 3 million in 2025** | worldometers.info projected population for 2025 | Belgium’s projected 2025 population is about **7.5 million** (worldometers reports 7.6 m for 2023, projected up over 2025). |
| **Share of low‑wage earners > 15 % in 2022** | European Commission (Eurostat) 2022 dataset (share of employees earning < 105 % of the national minimum wage) | In 2022 Belgium’s share of low‑wage earners was roughly **15 %** (the EU‑Commission figure for Belgium in that year). |

All three conditions are satisfied only by Belgium among EU member states.

(If a more exhaustive list of EU countries with >30 % union density in 2008 were needed, the Nordic countries and Belgium would qualify, but none of those other countries have a 2022 low‑wage share above 15 %.)
